name: Sony FE 100mm F2.8 Macro GM OSS
notes: The listed lens exists and is the current Sony macro G Master, so it was researched instead of the FE 90mm F2.8 Macro G OSS. Announced in autumn 2025 (the research pass gave September 2025, but the listed PetaPixel review is dated 9 October 2025, so the exact month is unconfirmed). Available November 2025 at approximately $1,499.99 USD (Sony). The elements/groups count (17 in 13), 0.26 m close focus, 1.4x magnification and 67 mm filter are nearly identical to Canon's RF100mm F2.8 L Macro IS USM. The audit could not re-check them against Sony's spec page, so treat them with some caution. Native magnification is 1.4x, up to 2.8x with an optional teleconverter (Sony). The lens has Optical SteadyShot, but Sony does not publish a CIPA stop rating in the sources found, so stops is null. No tripod collar (reviews), so the 646 g weight is lens only. The minimum working distance of about 90 mm at 1.4x, the 160-degree focus ring rotation and the focus-breathing remarks come from reviews.
famousFor: Sony's first G Master macro lens, notable for going beyond life-size to 1.4x magnification natively (2.8x with a teleconverter) while adding fast linear-motor AF and optical stabilisation.
strengths: 1.4x native maximum magnification, beyond the usual 1:1 of macro lenses
Very sharp at all focus distances, with clearly better edges than Sony's older 90mm macro
Fast, quiet autofocus from four XD linear motors driving a floating focus group
Teleconverter compatible, reaching up to 2.8x magnification
weaknesses: Focus breathing changes subject size when refocusing, so focus stacks need some cropping

No tripod collar, and priced well above typical 100mm macro lenses
bestFor: Beyond life-size macro of insects and small flowers

Tight headshot portraits with shallow depth of field
Close-up detail shots at weddings, such as rings and invitations
